Name: Shaikh Patta
site_type_note: A dargah/mazar as Shah Abdul Latif of Bhit records it; the present structure is not described.
_name_ur: Shaikh Patta, "Shaikh of Shaikhs" — shrine at Tatta. STRONGEST CANDIDATE FOR A FUTURE ROW.
_review: the line names saint, shrine and place: "the shrine of Shaikh Patta, Shaikh of Shaikhs" at Tatta, with the darwishes' dance before it (pp. 168-169, 298); "(i.e. in Tatta)" at p. 298 is Sorley's own interpolation; no death date, silsila or custodian on the line

Name: Sayid Muhammad Husain (Pir Murad)
site_type_note: A dargah/mazar as Shah Abdul Latif of Bhit records it; the present structure is not described.
_name_ur: Sayid Muhammad Husain, called Pir Murad, called Murad Buksh Shah — tomb in Tatta. SECOND STRONGEST CANDIDATE.
_review: "whose tomb is in Tatta" (p. 257); the book's index sends his third name-form "Murad Buksh Shah" to "(See Lal Shahbaz)" (p. 438), an unresolved collision the line itself records, hence the flag against lal-shahbaz-qalandar (Sehwan); no death date or silsila on the line; may be the same as lal-shahbaz-qalandar: kept apart, not merged
